clue.text: Sign, say, over vehicle

indicators.note: in a clue, over can mean turned over, so the abbreviation for say is written backwards

parts.note: EG (exempli gratia) is the abbreviation meaning say or for example
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: Someone notes a sign, perhaps a road sign, sitting above a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is the reversal signal, not a position word; 'Sign' looks like a road sign but is a zodiac sign.
explanation.definitionFit: The Twins is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac, between Taurus and Cancer.

clue.text: Inquisition victim, young woman associated with international sign

parts.note: gal is a colloquial word for a girl or young woman
Leo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A young woman tied to an international sign is a victim of the Inquisition.
explanation.definitionFit: The astronomer was tried by the Roman Inquisition in 1633 for supporting a sun-centred cosmos.

clue.text: Force could, possibly

definitions.meaning: noun: strength or power, as in with all one's strength
the past of may, meaning possibly could, as in it could rain

explanation.surface: Force might possibly work, someone suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Power and strength are one sense; the modal verb expressing possibility is the other.

clue.text: In no case loose the rein

indicators.note: loose means set free and scattered, so these letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to a rider: on no account let the reins go slack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' rearranges THE REIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Not either one of two options means in no case, as in 'in neither case'.

clue.text: Park employee called King Edward?

parts.note: called on the telephone, past tense, gives RANG
a king named Edward signs himself Edward Rex, abbreviated ER

explanation.surface: A park warden phoned in, giving his name as King Edward, the potato perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is also a British potato variety, which the question mark plays on; here it gives ER, Edwardus Rex.
explanation.definitionFit: A warden who looks after a national park or forest is employed under this job title.

clue.text: God represented by parrot wearing a ring

indicators.note: wearing means the parrot sits within a and the ring, as if dressed in them

parts.note: a ring is round, shaped like the letter O
Poll is a traditional name for a pet parrot

explanation.surface: A god represented in art by a parrot wearing a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts POLL inside A and O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek deity of music, poetry and the sun is one of the Olympians.

clue.text: Impertinence shown by terrible old ruler — time to run around

parts.note: gall is cheek or impertinence
Ivan the Terrible was a sixteenth-century tsar of Russia

explanation.surface: A cheeky old tyrant says it is time to dash about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' looks like an adjective but points to the Russian tsar Ivan the Terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: To go about seeking pleasure is to roam or gad about.

clue.text: Artist, British actor and, finally, Francis Bacon

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
Sir Antony Sher was a British actor

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A list of artists and actors, ending with the painter Francis Bacon.
explanation.walkthrough: Francis Bacon reads as the painter, but Francis only gives its final S and Bacon is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Slices of bacon are rashers, so the plural fits bacon on the breakfast plate.

clue.text: Crude hooligan, Desperate Dan, has cash

parts.note: a rough is a violent hooligan

indicators.note: desperate suggests things are wild and in disarray, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the ready, or readies, is slang for cash

explanation.surface: Desperate Dan, the comic-strip strongman, is a crude hooligan with money.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a British comic character; 'Desperate' rearranges DAN to AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic and makeshift but serviceable, unrefined, is crude in this sense.

clue.text: Work away, almost leisurely, to get a lot of money

indicators.note: almost means the word falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: leisurely means slow, unhurried
G stands for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Advice to work steadily, almost at a relaxed pace, in order to earn a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last letter from SLOW, leaving SLO.
explanation.definitionFit: To plod on at hard, tiring labour is to toil away at it steadily.

clue.text: Denouncer's unorthodox antics 'cool'

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition Denouncer to the wordplay

indicators.note: unorthodox means not following the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic's odd behaviour is dismissed by someone as 'cool'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unorthodox' shuffles the ten letters of ANTICS and COOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who attacks cherished beliefs or institutions is a denouncer of them, a breaker of idols.

clue.text: Bit of a mishap: Grand Canal emptied and burning

indicators.note: emptied means the inside of the phrase is removed, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: a burning desire or burning sensation is an itch

explanation.surface: A small accident in Venice: the Grand Canal drained and something on fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emptied' strips everything but the outer letters of the whole phrase Grand Canal, G and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor malfunction or hitch is a small fault, a slight setback rather than a disaster.

clue.text: Pull back, being a much-travelled character

indicators.note: back tells us to write the word for pull in reverse

parts.note: to lug is to pull or drag something heavy
one who lives, a being, is a liver

explanation.surface: Someone retreating, being a character who has seen a great deal of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses LUG to GUL; LIVER is the rare sense 'one who lives', not the organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift's hero sails to Lilliput, Brobdingnag and other strange lands in his famous Travels.

clue.text: Energy-packed NCO material

indicators.note: packed means the energy symbol is stuffed inside the rank

parts.note: a corporal is a non-commissioned officer
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A soldier's kit or uniform cloth stuffed with energy, perhaps a new fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packed' puts E into CORPORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Material in the sense of physical or bodily, as opposed to spiritual, is the adjective here.

clue.text: Obvious liar about to cut Chopin composition, Zeus's lover

indicators.note: to cut means the abbreviation for about slices into the rearranged composer
a composition is something composed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
Io was a mortal loved by Zeus and turned into a heifer

explanation.surface: A liar abridging a Chopin piece, then a mention of Zeus's mistress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' rearranges CHOPIN to PINOCH; 'to cut' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The wooden puppet's nose grows whenever he tells a lie, so his lies show.

clue.text: World title cracked by amateur

indicators.note: cracked by means the title is broken open with the amateur letter inside

parts.note: Mrs is a title given to a married woman

explanation.surface: A world championship won by an amateur who broke through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracked by' puts A inside MRS.
explanation.definitionFit: The red planet is one of the worlds of the solar system.

clue.text: Don Juan's undone and missing a godly partner

indicators.note: undone suggests the letters of the name are unpicked and reassembled
missing says the letters of the following word are absent from the jumble

explanation.surface: The famous seducer has been ruined and lost a partner who was devout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undone' rearranges DONJUAN; 'missing' takes A, N and D out of it, leaving four letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman queen of the gods was wife to Jupiter, a partner to a god.

clue.text: Vessel on which folk duo member found objects of rubbish

parts.note: a junk is a Chinese sailing ship
Art Garfunkel was half of the folk duo Simon and Garfunkel

explanation.surface: On a ship, a folk singer finds some rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found objects' is the art term for everyday items used in artworks.
explanation.definitionFit: Sculpture and collage made from scrap and discarded things are works using found objects.

clue.text: Qualifier, Jet, overwhelmed with advice

indicators.note: overwhelmed suggests being knocked over and thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sports qualifier called Jet is swamped with advice from coaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overwhelmed' shuffles JET and ADVICE.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, a describing word qualifies a noun, so it is a qualifier.

clue.text: Term wasted with eel that's prone to disease

indicators.note: wasted means ruined, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A sickly eel's term ends in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' rearranges TERM and EEL; the definition alludes to Dutch elm disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutch elm disease killed most of Britain's elms in the 1970s, so the tree is notoriously susceptible.

clue.text: Drake versus duck with a grey cast?

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of nothing, O

indicators.note: cast means thrown about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drake squares up to a duck with grey colouring.
explanation.walkthrough: Drake is not a male duck but Sir Francis Drake; 'cast' rearranges A GREY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elizabethan sea captain sailed around the world, so he was a great seafarer.

clue.text: Marauding type of short woman married to ruler

parts.note: Vi is a short form of the name Violet or Victoria
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A small woman with a looting streak married a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short woman' reads as small in stature but means a shortened name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse seafarers raided coasts across Europe, so they were plunderers.

clue.text: Trials take place here shortly — one has to be still

parts.note: trials are held in a court, and shortly abbreviates court to CT, giving in a CT
one has can be written I have, contracted to I've

explanation.surface: A short description of a courtroom, where someone must stay motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: Trials take place in a court; 'shortly' abbreviates court to its usual short form CT. 'one has' is the contraction I've.
explanation.definitionFit: Being motionless or doing nothing is the opposite of active, a synonym of not moving.

clue.text: For example, Sebastian Drive, backing onto ancient city (not eastern)

indicators.note: backing means the word for drive is written backwards

parts.note: to ram is to drive or force something in

indicators.note: not eastern removes E, the abbreviation for east

parts.note: Tyre is an ancient Phoenician city in modern Lebanon

explanation.surface: A street address: Sebastian Drive, backing onto the remains of an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses RAM to MAR; 'not eastern' drops E from TYRE. Sebastian Drive looks like a street name.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Sebastian was killed for his Christian faith, famously shot with arrows, so he died for his beliefs.

clue.text: Dog collar's hem old parson turned up?

indicators.note: the hem is the edge, here the final letter of collar
in a down entry, turned up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for reverend, is a clergyman

explanation.surface: Was the hem of a dog collar turned up by an old parson?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog collar' suggests a clerical collar but Dog is the definition; 'turned up' reverses REV to VER.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional name for a pet dog, as in Spot or Fido.

clue.text: Pioneer father secures source of hieroglyphic discovery

indicators.note: secures means the word for father holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: pater is Latin for father, used in English too

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a find is a discovery

explanation.surface: A pioneering father makes a discovery that begins with hieroglyphics, an Egyptologist perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'father' is the Latin pater, not dad or pa; 'secures' holds the H, from 'source of' hieroglyphic, and the discovery inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer explores new ground ahead of others, finding a route for them.

clue.text: Greens getting a conspicuous star

parts.note: greens are vegetables, shortened to veg

explanation.surface: A vegetable dish becomes the star attraction of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The brightest star in the constellation Lyra is one of the most prominent in the night sky.

clue.text: Roger, protected by criminal, arrives at low point

indicators.note: protected by means the criminal surrounds Roger, keeping it inside

parts.note: a tough is a violent criminal or thug
in radio talk, Roger means received, abbreviated R

explanation.surface: Roger, guarded by a crook, reaches a low ebb in his fortunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protected by' puts R inside TOUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest point in a cycle, as in economic peaks and dips, is the bottom of a wave.

clue.text: Alarm — time to put on slip

indicators.note: to put on means the time letter is placed before the slip, in front of it

parts.note: a slip is a mistake or error

explanation.surface: An alarm goes off: time to put on a slip, a petticoat, and get dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put on' places T in front of ERROR. 'slip' poses as an undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: Great fear or fright is alarm in its sense of sudden dread.
